objetivo.exact: Infrastructure then becomes that which channels, defines, contains, capitalises the always excessive flows of affective intensity, an intensity materialised in various substances and compositions. Infrastructure can be read as the embodiment of specific instantiations of capital flows, the aspirations of various kinds of articulation, the concretisation of accords, as strategic devices for socialising bodies and places, and as technologies for 'throwntogetherness' (Massey, 2005).

nfrastructure embodies particular dispositions (Easterling, 2014), particular capacities to operate on and effect users in specific ways as a kind of power in readiness. It lures and inclines, and we, in return are inclined toward it so that a holding takes place. So captivation can become capture, and we are subject to the extraction of our attention and energies.

Our everyday routines and itineraries constantly skirt on the interface between habituation and improvisation, where improvisation entails knowing from where we set off from but always raises that question about how to get 'home'.

objetivo.exact: Instigating infrastructure and the rush to build. So here, I want to emphasise how infrastructure enacts a seemingly contradictory 'doubleness' of temporality: it attempts to stabilise the volatility of the present and instigate a volatility of the future.

What AbdouMaliq and I are arguing is that by paying attention to infrastructure we see the kind of trans-individual ground from which politics emerges, for what counts as politics and what doesn't count as politics. It's not that every kind of politics is encompassed within attention to infrastructure.
